content:
Ethan Wallace: hey @Jonas Weber @Claire Dubois — can we get a few chart snapshots for the report draft by EOD tomorrow? looking for: (1) latency/$ by model x region (main hero), (2) p95 latency heatmap, (3) $/1M tokens bar for the top 6 models. doesn’t need to be final-polished, just “good enough to write to”

Soojin Lee: +1. also, for each chart can you include what we should annotate re: variance + methodology caveats? we’re getting feedback that we need to be explicit about confidence/stability so it doesn’t read like cherry-picking.

Alicia Perez: jumping in — for layout i need aspect ratio + rough dimensions. if you can export 16:9 and also a square crop it helps. png ok.

Jonas Weber: yep. we can export from the notebook as static PNGs. question: do you want “single best run” or aggregated? (we should not use single best, but want to confirm)

Ethan Wallace: aggregated please. whatever the methodology doc says is the “publishable” number.

Claire Dubois: publishable is aggregated across repeated runs after warmup w/ stability gate. (we’re doing min 5 runs per model/region/config; more if variance trips the gate). we can add error bars but it may clutter.

Ben Carter: from growth POV: we’ll reuse these in email + social. we need something legible on mobile. maybe better to annotate w/ a footnote like “shaded band indicates run-to-run variance” vs full errorbars everywhere.

Wei Chen: +1 to footnote/tooltips approach. on the landing page we can have tooltip copy like “Each point is median of N runs. We rerun if p95 varies > X%.” what’s the actual X?

Rina Kobayashi: stability gate right now: auto-rerun if p95 latency differs by >12% across runs for same model/region/config. also exclude runs with infra incidents or capacity throttling flags. (we track this in the manifest)

Jonas Weber: we also have per-run sample size: 10k requests total per config, with concurrency profile mix. we can share N requests + N runs in a caption.

Soojin Lee: perfect. can you also confirm how we’re handling caching/batching? we need to preempt “you turned on magic caching” accusations.

Claire Dubois: we’re using Redwood’s default production serving config (continuous batching on; KV cache enabled as applicable; prompt cache OFF unless explicitly stated). no prompt-prefix cache on this dataset. we should say that clearly. also note: results depend on request mix (prefill/decode distribution).

Ethan Wallace: can we get a one-liner for the chart caption like: “Median across repeated sweeps; shaded region is p25–p75 across runs; rerun on high variance.” is p25–p75 what you’re actually outputting?

Jonas Weber: we can output p25/p75 across runs for each point, yes. if we don’t do shading, we can still provide the numbers for the methodology appendix.

Alicia Perez: if we do shading, i can keep it subtle (10–15% opacity). but we need to make sure it doesn’t imply “statistical CI” unless it actually is.

Michael Grant: (legal) +1. please avoid calling it “confidence interval” unless it’s a real CI w/ assumptions stated. “run-to-run variability” / “inter-run range” is safer.

Soojin Lee: noted. we’ll use “run-to-run variability” language.

Wei Chen: also for p95 heatmap, do we annotate “measured at X concurrency” and “streaming on/off”? otherwise ppl will assume apples-to-apples across everything.

Rina Kobayashi: p95 heatmap is for chat completions w/ streaming ON, concurrency profile ‘prod-mix-v3’ (peaks at 32 concurrent). we’ll include that in the caption.

Ben Carter: can we add a small callout somewhere: “Your mileage will vary by prompt + token lengths; replicate w/ our harness”? we’ve had a few comments on other launches about that.

Claire Dubois: yes. we can add a standard caveat block:
- workload = prompt-set-v3 production mix (prefill+decode)
- fixed input/output token buckets
- regional results reflect available capacity during the run window
- reruns triggered on p95 variance threshold

Jonas Weber: sharing WIP exports tomorrow morning. where should i drop? drive folder?

Ethan Wallace: drop in the GTM shared drive under /go-to-market/benchmark-report-charts-scratchpad (same place as the sketches). link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/REDACTED

Alicia Perez: pls name files w/ figure ids so i can track them in layout. like `fig-2-latency-per-dollar-by-region.png`, `fig-4-p95-heatmap.png`.

Soojin Lee: and if you can include a small text blob w/ each export: “what it shows + how to read + caveats.” we’ll paste into tooltips.

Jonas Weber: ok. i’ll export:
1) latency/$: scatter (model) w/ facet by region + shading = inter-run p25–p75
2) p95 heatmap: model x region, legend in ms, note concurrency + streaming
3) $/1M tokens: bars for top models, using same workload + pricing assumptions doc

Michael Grant: one more request: please include the exact date range of the sweep in the caption metadata (e.g., “runs executed 2025-06-04 to 2025-06-06”). helps w/ substantiation.

Claire Dubois: we have that per manifest; we’ll include run window in the caption pack.

Wei Chen: question: do we want to annotate “we exclude outliers from incidents” on the chart itself or only methodology?

Soojin Lee: methodology + footnote on landing page. chart itself should stay readable.

Ethan Wallace: +1. keep chart clean, put caveats in caption + methodology.

Rina Kobayashi: FYI for anyone writing tooltip copy: we don’t ‘drop’ outliers arbitrarily; we mark runs invalid if they have explicit incident flags (5xx spike, throttling, degraded region) or failed stability gate. everything else is included.

Ben Carter: that’s good wording. we’ll use “invalid runs removed per predefined criteria” not “outliers removed.”

Jonas Weber: cool. will deliver tomorrow ~10am PT.

Alicia Perez: :eyes: thanks. ping me when uploaded.

Soojin Lee: thanks all. after we have snapshots, i’ll do a quick pass w/ Legal on the exact caveat phrasing for “variance” so it’s consistent across web/PDF/blog.

Michael Grant: appreciated. just route the final caption language; we can review fast if it matches the guidelines.

Ethan Wallace: perfect. closing the loop tomorrow once figs are in.
